Let the polynomial degree be $\qp \geq 1$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ and $q \geq 2$ for $d=3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate ||I_h p_tt - p_tt||_{L^2} \lesssim h^q ||p_tt||_{H^q} applies Lemma lem: local interpolant properties with n = q = 1, i = 0, l = 2 in d = 2, but that lemma requires n - d/l > 0, i.e., q > d/2. At d = 2, q = 1 one has q = d/2 = 1, violating the hypothesis. Since the regularity assumption p in H^2(0,T; H^q cap L^infty) gives only p_tt in H^q = H^1, the value n = q+1 is unavailable. At the borderline n = d/l the Lagrange-type continuous interpolant is not guaranteed to be well-defined because H^1(Omega) does not embed into C^0 for d = 2, and the interpolation estimate has no uniform constant at this threshold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the polynomial-degree hypothesis to q_p > d/2 (requiring q_p >= 2 when d = 2), which excludes only the case d = 2, q_p = 1 while preserving the method and optimal rate in every other regime. Alternatively, replace the Lagrange-type interpolant with a boundary-robust operator (e.g., Scott-Zhang) in the estimate of I_h p_tt - p_tt to cover the borderline case without losing any parameter regime.
issues.overall_effect: For d = 2 and q_p = 1 the defect bound in Lemma lem: bound defect, the uniform discrete error estimate in Proposition prop: nonlin error bound, the global existence and optimal energy-norm error bound in Theorem thm: wellposedness nonlin, and the concentration error bound in Theorem thm: full model concentration are all unsupported. All results remain proved for d = 2 with q_p >= 2 and for d in {1,3} with the stated polynomial degrees.
issues.title: Interpolation estimate for second time derivative of interpolation error unjustified at borderline regularity for d=2, q=1
issues.why_classification: Either repair preserves the method, convergence rate, and all results outside a single excluded parameter case and requires no new global proof architecture. Restricting the degree is a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result; switching the interpolant is a contained nontrivial modification. Neither resolution causes major mathematical loss.
